The 8 Best Outdoor Security Cameras Keep an Eye on Your Home When You're Away

📅 29 Mar 2021 | ⏱️ 18 min read (3674 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popularmechanics

⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review.
  • Keeping your home safe these days takes more than a deadbolt and a dog with a menacing bark.
  • Outdoor security cameras in particular are your best bet to prevent break-ins.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

Keeping your home safe these days takes more than a deadbolt and a dog with a menacing bark. Installing a few security cameras around your property is an easy and surprisingly cost-effective way to level up your home security, adding watchful eyes that track comings and goings 24/7. Until relatively recently, the only options for personal home security were comprehensive (and expensive) systems that were installed and monitored by security professionals. Now, you can set up your own cameras and home security system that saves you cash without sacrificing performance.

Outdoor security cameras in particular are your best bet to prevent break-ins. According to Security.org, simply having a clearly visible camera or security device on your property serves as a strong deterrent for trespassers. Outdoor security cameras are equipped with features found in indoor security cameras like high-definition video, night vision, two-way audio, and more. In addition to this, they come equipped with outdoor-specific features like weather-resistant exteriors, sound detection, and integrated motion-activated spotlights.

According to recent reports, for this guide, we got our hands on the most promising options from well-established brands including Arlo, Wyze, Ring, and Eufy and tested them at our homes and offices. Read on below to learn about the best outdoor security cameras we recommend, along with expert advice to help you choose the right option for your home and budget.

One quick note before we dive in: It’s increasingly vital to pick security gear that’s compatible with whatever smart home system you already have. For example, Amazon makes it easy to pull up a live feed from your Ring camera(s) on an Echo Show or Fire TV and has designed its products to more seamlessly connect with its other smart home devices. Same goes for Google products. If you already have a few items from a major smart home brand, consider buying gear that will be as compatible as possible with it.

More Home Improvement Stories: Best Retractable Awnings ● The Popular Mechanics 2025 Yard & Garden Awards ● Best Solar-Powered Outdoor Lights.

According to recent reports, we selected our recommendations based on a round of substantial testing: We installed these cameras outdoors, and used them to survey our homes for weeks, and in some cases months. We watched them as they watched our properties, as they endured a wide spectrum of outdoor conditions including snow and rain.

We tested and compared their basic video recording functionality, evaluating them on clarity, field of view, and weather resistance as well as any special features they offer like spotlights, solar charging, sirens, and more. Some of the cameras on this list were tested in outdoor settings for months, facing a wide spectrum of outdoor conditions including snow and rain.

We also tested their more nuanced security and tech features, including motion detection notifications, AI recognition of animals and packages, two-way audio conversations, and digital borders, among others. These features were considered as well as the cost, if any, associated with buying access to all of them.

We recommended the Wyze Outdoor Cam V2 ahead of testing, based on its low price, solid specs, and the past performance of other Wyze cameras that we've tested.

Recent findings suggest that the Arlo Essential XL stands out for its user-friendly design, durable exterior, and of course, its clear video quality—all for a fair price. It's completely wireless, which means you can mount it anywhere around your home without worrying about power and wiring issues.

It excels as a 24/7 outdoor cam, with features like color night vision that improves the clarity of nighttime footage. During testing, we were impressed by its resolution in low light, as well as its accurate motion detection. It provides real-time alerts directly to your smartphone, and will let you check a live feed to observe any suspicious activity live as it happens.

Sources indicate that you can also program the integrated spotlight to automatically flash on when someone is within visual range. It's a great deterrent against potential robberies, and lets you leave the house without leaving a porch light on.

While this cam has solid features without a subscription, an Arlo Secure subscription adds cloud storage for your video footage, as well as additional target recognition and home security features, for $96 to $300 per year.

Arlo Essential XL Security Camera Review.

Few options balance price and quality as well as this affordable option from Wyze. The battery-operated Wyze Outdoor V2 camera can be mounted anywhere. New buyers should pick up the starter kit, which includes a base unit that allows you to expand your system with up to four cameras.

Though it's the most affordable on the list, it still offers a lineup of powerful features including motion-sensing technology that detects both body heat and movement, reducing the number of potential false alarms drastically.

The Wyze is also quite flexible for storage options with the camera capable of online cloud storage as well as localized storage on a microSD card.

Solar-powered cameras, while power-efficient, present extra setup challenges. Most of the time, the panel is attached to the body of the camera, so you need to need find to camera positions with a good field of view and get good sun exposure. Depending on the layout of your home and the surrounding area, that may lead to less-than-ideal placements, which create holes in your surveillance.

The Tapo MagCam solves this problem with a detachable solar panel, so you can keep it connected when it's effective, or remove and mount it higher above the camera to get more sun. It features a 13-foot extension cord, so you have a good amount of slack to move it to an open, sunshiny space.

In a recent development, test Editor Bradley Ford mounted his test camera in a semi-shaded area, then set up the solar panel in direct sunlight. Despite the fact that he was testing at the end of 2025, when there was significantly less daily sunlight, the battery never dipped below 80 percent charge. In the warmer weather, the camera typically sat at 100 percent.

In addition, Ford preferred that the MagCam relied on local storage. "One of the things we like best is that there is no need for a subscription to access activation videos," Ford noted. "They’re all stored locally on a Micro SD card in the camera. However, if you wish to pay for cloud storage, that option is also available.".

This specific kit comes with a camera, solar panel, and mount, however Tapo offers others with two or three cameras as well.

It has been revealed that our previous pick in this category, the Ring Floodlight Cam Wired Plus, was a terrific outdoor security camera that featured a dual-LED floodlight. The new Ring Floodlight Cam Wired Pro builds on that solid design with extra features, including support for dual-band WiFi and a “bird’s-eye view” feature that tracks a recorded subject as they move within the camera’s view, showing it on a top-down layout of the area.

The camera’s 1080p video resolution and 140-degree field of view are the same as the previous model, but image quality is enhanced with high dynamic range (HDR) support, which improves visibility in both low light and extremely bright conditions.

The lights themselves are also quite bright, 2000 lumens each, and the fixtures are adjustable so you can angle the light as you please.

The Ring Floodlight Cam Wired Pro also features two-way audio support, with a 110-decibel siren that sounds when the system detects motion. It also offers customizable motion zones and 3D- motion radar for you to tailor to your property.

A word of warning: We found the wired installation was fairly difficult, so we recommend hiring an electrician unless you're experienced with wiring and up for a challenge.

Unlike any other outdoor security camera on our list, this option from Tactacam does not require a WiFi connection. Instead, it connects to cellular towers and works similarly to your smartphone. This makes the camera perfect for homes in remote locations.

The security camera does require a monthly subscription for access to on-demand videos and photos that are stored in the cloud, but prepares start at just 5 bucks a month.

Recent findings suggest that the device works with AA batteries or a rechargeable battery pack. In our testing, we took anywhere from two to 10 pictures a day and the pack lasted about three to four months before needing to be recharged.

Sources indicate that in practice, the security camera is great at sensing motion more than 100 feet away, so it could potentially double as a nature cam. It lacks some of the features other, similarly priced models on this list have, but the biggest drawback is that the field of view is only about 50 feet wide.

The Arlo floodlight has everything we love from our top pick, including Arlo's superior app and software, but adds on a large floodlight, as well as a need for wired power.

In a recent development, as with the Arlo Essential XL, you get quality motion detection software and color night vision. Spring for Arlo Secure, and you get AI target recognition that can point out passing cars or faces, and highlight packages.

The floodlight also has some interesting features: Each light is individually adjustable, so you can angle them for the best possible coverage. That includes creative solutions like angling one light toward your back door, while pointing the other toward the steps leading to your back porch. It's a small touch, but a very appreciated one. It also includes a loud, 110-decibel siren.

If you're looking for a low-maintenance outdoor security camera system, eufy's S330 "eufycam 3" is a dynamic wireless option that supports solar charging and doesn't require professional installation.

Once installed and set up, we did not have to take either of the cameras down for recharging once over months of use. The solar panels kept them perpetually charged as long as they got exposure to a few hours of sunlight per day.

Industry observers note that it was similarly easy to connect the cameras to the greater home security. The outdoor cameras works through the home hub which after initial installation using an ethernet cable, works comfortably through your home WiFi. The cameras can then be set up anywhere within several hundred feet of the hub without losing connection.

According to recent reports, A big benefit we also loved is the camera system requires no monthly subscription to access its features. This includes AI-powered face recognition, customizable activity zones, and of course, motion detection.

The only drawback for this camera set is the placement of the solar panels. While the panels being integrated directly on top of the camera makes it less cumbersome, it also means you need to install them in a spot with direct sunlight or they won't properly charge.

It has been revealed that the Reolink Argus 4 Pro gives you a sweeping 180-degree field of view, which allows you to cover large open spaces with as few cameras as possible. Properly positioned, you can achieve a near-complete view of an area with just two cameras.

According to recent reports, this 4K camera features a dual-lens design that covers larger areas without blind spots or fishbowl-style warping. You'd think that might lead to complications with position or usage, but we found it easy to operate.

Sources indicate that it features discrete solar panels for power, which allows for more placement flexibility: For example, you can install the camera under a ledge or rooftop, then secure the solar panel above, where it will get direct sun. That makes it easier to get the perfect shot and optimal power.

In terms of storage, the Argus 4 Pro records footage locally and connects to a home hub. You don't have to pay a monthly fee for cloud storage or additional features. Simply turn it on, connect it the hub, and in theory, it should run without concern in perpetuity.

There are two types of consumer-grade home security cameras: wireless battery-powered cameras that you can set up easily nearly anywhere, but require you to occasionally replace batteries, and wired models that connect directly to your home's electrical system.

It has been revealed that wired cameras are generally more expensive and require an electrician's help unless you're comfortable with home wiring, but require far less maintenance once they're installed. Their placement is also restricted to locations where you can wired them in.

Battery-powered cameras, by contrast, are only restricted by the range of your WiFi router. Of course, you'll need to access them every few months to replace their batteries. Some models feature solar panels, giving you renewable energy, but panels also impose some placement restrictions. (Namely, access to sunlight).

It has been revealed that wired cameras do fall short of battery-powered models in one niche scenario—when the power goes out. Unlike, say, wired smoke or carbon monoxide detectors, which have reliable battery backup, you can't count on a wired security camera to provide surveillance footage during an extended period of time if there's a power failure. It varies from model to model, but most wired cameras can only last for 30 minutes to, at most, a few hours before they go dark.

Sources indicate that to avoid recording 24/7, which wastes power and storage space, outdoor security cameras usually feature motion sensors that trigger recording whenever there’s activity. Many cameras will also an alert to your companion app whenever they start recording.

Most cameras give you the ability to calibrate the motion sensor by setting motion zones in spots where you expect frequent false alarms, like a sidewalk. Others offer smart features that can differentiate between people, animals, and vehicles. You should also have the ability to customize your notifications, so you’ll only receive an alert in certain situations, like if it detects a person.

Furthermore, some cameras feature microphones, enabling audio detection, which can trigger recording and alerts based on nearby sounds that may be out of view (like a window breaking). Audio detection is a useful extra layer in a few specific situations, like when a single camera can’t cover the entire side of your home, but may also lead to more nuisance alerts. If you decide to use one, we recommend customizing your audio alert sensitivity if possible so you aren’t constantly getting notified when the neighbor’s dog barks.

The best outdoor security cameras record video in "Full HD" (1920 x 1080p) resolution, which captures enough detail to identify facial features or a car’s license plate. More expensive cameras record at higher resolutions, such as 2K or "Quad HD" (2560 x 1440p) or 4K Ultra HD (3840 x 2160) video, which deliver better detail. While higher resolution may help, 1080p video is usually clear enough to give you more than enough information in most situations.

Sources indicate that your camera’s field of view (FOV) is just as notable as its resolution. Field of view refers to how wide of an angle the lens is and therefore, how much of your yard or porch is in view. With a wider FOV, your camera can see a wider area around your property, providing more coverage. For the best results, we recommend a model with a field of view between 130 and 180 degrees.

Many outdoor cameras also feature an integrated spotlight that can illuminate the surroundings if motion is detected, improving visibility in low-light situations. A spotlight also acts as a deterrent by making potential intruders more visible. Similarly, the majority of outdoor cameras offer some kind of night vision feature, which uses infrared (IR) lights to record a high-contrast black and white video in the dark. Top-of-the-line cameras are capable of recording standard video in low light, minimizing the need for night vision.

According to recent reports, there’s no point in recording camera footage if you can’t store it for when you need it. Many manufacturers offer free cloud storage for a limited time—typically seven days–after which video is overwritten with new recordings. You can always download and save that footage, so long as you do during that initial window.

If you want to save your footage for a longer period, there are a couple of options. Many companies provide additional cloud storage for a subscription fee. There are also cameras that feature a microSD card slot for storing footage locally. This does require a bit of extra maintenance in the form of occasionally removing the card and either deleting or downloading the recorded data to free up more space on the card.

According to recent reports, if you’re concerned with privacy, be aware that cloud footage is generally kept on a manufacturer’s servers, which can be stolen if the company’s digital security is breached. Some companies may also use or share data from stored recordings in ways you might not anticipate. For example, Amazon has shared footage from Ring cameras to law enforcement without customers’ permission on many occasions. While storing locally requires more legwork, it is definitely the most secure option for privacy-conscious homeowners.

It has been revealed that security cameras are more than just their features. Nearly all security cameras are built to connect with other smart home devices. So, before buying any specific option, make sure it is compatible with the devices you already own. For example, Amazon makes it easy to pull up a live feed from your Ring camera(s) on an Echo Show or Fire TV. There are many brands that work with the majority of the smart home software available such as Apple, Google Nest, and Ring. Some have limited functionality on other smart home software systems outside of their brand, but still work with them. Furthermore, most security camera brands require a monthly subscription to gain full access to many of their features. These monthly subscriptions range in price and overall necessity with some basically essential to operate the cameras and store footage in the cloud while others are designed as a bonus add-on to the base product. Prior to purchase, make sure to take a close look at both the smart home compatibility as well as what comes with and without the monthly subscription service.

Most of the outdoor security cameras we recommend are sold individually or as part of a larger set. The number of cameras you need for your property will vary, based on your home security initiative and how much camera coverage you want. A well-installed camera with a wide field of view can cover an important and vulnerable area on your property, such as a back door or garage.

In a recent development, that said, even a small home will need at least a few cameras to achieve full coverage on every ground-level door and window. You may need multiple cameras to reveal tricky blind spots created by corners, lawn features, and anything else that might impede a single camera position.

It has been revealed that don't freak out about needing a fleet of surveillance gear, though. Not everyone wants or needs to have every single square inch of their property under constant watch. It’s up to you to decide where you want an extra eye. The important thing is to make sure you know what you need before making a purchase.

Recent findings suggest that of course. There are no features of an outdoor security camera that would prevent it from working inside. That noted, many companies make indoor cameras that are cheaper, and may feature a stand or mounting options that make more sense for blending in with your home or office.

You should always be careful when considering home security. Over the years, there have been multiple reports of strangers accessing live video feeds and recorded videos from home security cameras.

Luckily, there are simple ways to protect yourself. As with other devices, adhering to digital security best practices, such as keeping your smart home devices’ firmware up to date, creating a strong password and activating two-factor authentication wherever possible, will help prevent a breach.

In a recent development, you may also have concerns about who has access to video that’s stored in the cloud. Most companies ask for permission to review recordings for research and development purposes. Depending on the company, this request often comes in the form of an “opt-in” setting in the camera app, though some may turn it on by default unless you “opt out.”.

Recent findings suggest that some may also share recordings with law enforcement. In some cases, they will only do so when compelled by a search warrant. A couple manufacturers, specifically Amazon (Ring) and Google (Nest), have noted they will provide footage without a warrant if law enforcement claims it is an emergency.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Robert Garcia, D-Calif., is expected to lead the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee.
  • The Trump administration signaled it would respond aggressively to a Democratic-led Congress with a letter this week threatening to prosecute lawmakers for oversight efforts.
  • The letter from White House Counsel Will Scharf sent Monday to House Oversight and Government Reform ranking member Robert Garcia, D-Calif., argued that members of Congress have limited authority to conduct oversight of a presidential administration and that some of the threats to glitch subpoenas “may cross the line into blatant criminality.”.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, rep. Robert Garcia, D-Calif., is expected to lead the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call file photo).

The Trump administration signaled it would respond aggressively to a Democratic-led Congress with a letter this week threatening to prosecute lawmakers for oversight efforts.

The letter from White House Counsel Will Scharf sent Monday to House Oversight and Government Reform ranking member Robert Garcia, D-Calif., argued that members of Congress have limited authority to conduct oversight of a presidential administration and that some of the threats to glitch subpoenas “may cross the line into blatant criminality.”.

The letter, obtained from a White House official, marks the latest escalation from the Trump administration ahead of Democrats taking control of both chambers of Congress next year. It also dovetails with years of Trump’s threats to prosecute his critics.

“We are monitoring the abusive and capricious threats that are now proliferating from Democrat legislators who seek to abuse the legislative process to intimidate and to interfere with the lawful functioning of government,” the letter claims.

Garcia, the likely committee chair next Congress, pushed back on the threat in a statement Wednesday, accusing the administration of having “something to hide” and that Congress has wide authority to investigate the executive branch.

Sources indicate that “The American people voted overwhelmingly for us to pass laws to root out corruption and abuse," Garcia said. "The Trump Administration continues to weaponize the government with threats of unconstitutional attacks on Congress. We are a co-equal branch of government and will not be deterred by baseless threats from a weaponized DOJ or from the President’s lawyers.”.

The letter came after Attorney General Todd Blanche previously refused to rule out criminal charges against members of Congress in response to investigations.

"It depends on what the crime is and what they have done,” Blanche told CNN over the weekend.

Last week, President Donald Trump himself noted that threats of investigations and impeachment were “extortion at the highest level” and called for the Justice Department to “look into this criminal act, immediately!”.

He also singled out Sen. Elissa Slotkin, D-Mich., calling for her to be imprisoned. The administration previously unsuccessfully attempted to indict Slotkin and other Democrats over a video she published calling for soldiers to disobey illegal orders.

And Trump last year publicly called for longtime critic Sen. Adam B. Schiff, D-Calif., to face unspecified charges in a post on Truth Social addressed to then-Attorney General Pam Bondi that also called for the prosecution of former FBI Director James Comey and Newly introduced York Attorney General Letitia James. Both have faced criminal charges, pleaded not guilty and fought them in court as political attacks.

Sources indicate that garcia and other Democrats have signaled they intend to pursue oversight aggressively in the new Congress. After Democrats won the House majority last week, Garcia put out an all-caps statement urging administration officials to “LAWYER UP” ahead of the new year.

In a recent development, garcia, as well as other likely incoming chairs such as House Judiciary ranking member Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md.; Homeland Security ranking member Rep. Bennie Thompson, D-Miss.; and Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., have hinted at broad inquiries ranging from the handling of files related to deceased sex offender Jeffrey Epstein to immigration enforcement and more.

Raskin told reporters last week that he thought Democratic oversight efforts could dovetail with the party’s broader effort to address affordability complications, including by addressing the Iran war, allegations of corruption within the Trump administration and more.

“We're going to get all the information that we need in order to restore the rule of law in American constitutional democracy,” Raskin noted.

The letter also echoes a previous fight the administration pitched with the House in the first Trump administration, where officials resisted in court allowing former White House Counsel Don McGahn to testify to the House Judiciary Committee for years.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A-Rosa has entered a strategic partnership with Columbia blue to strengthen crew management and onboard hotel services across the European river cruise fleet.

Starting at the beginning of 2027, the Columbia signature brand will take responsibility for selected hotel crew recruitment administration and operational hotel services across the A-Rosa fleet operating on the Rhine, Danube, Rhône and Seine rivers.

The collaboration is designed to strengthen operational stability, broaden access to qualified personnel and support the long-term growth ambitions of A-Rosa, according to a press release.

Rolf-Dieter Maltzahn, CEO of A-Rosa, said: “With Columbia blue, we are combining the brand and product expertise of A-Rosa with international recruitment and hospitality expertise. In this way, we are strengthening the continuous ability to offer our future guests the quality and personal travel experience that A-Rosa stands for.”.

Under the agreement, A-Rosa will retain its vertically integrated business model, including its own tour operator, shipping company and fleet, maintaining full responsibility for strategic direction, brand positioning, product development, quality standards and the guest experience.

Columbia blue will complement this by providing specialist operational services, with A-Rosa remaining the framework for all onboard hotel operations.

“A-Rosa has a strong brand, a distinct product promise and extensive experience in the European river cruise market. We look forward to contributing our expertise and working together to develop an efficient and resilient model for hotel services,’’ noted Norman Schmiedl, CEO of Columbia blue.

The agreement comes as the increase in capacity, upcoming market entrants and intensifying competition for experienced hospitality professionals across the European river cruise sector place greater demands on operators to secure skilled personnel.

Windstar Cruises completed its third Mystery Cruise, an eight-night journey along Spain’s coast aboard the Star Legend.

Sailing from Barcelona to Málaga November 4–12, 2026, the voyage took travelers to a series of surprise destinations, giving them clues for each destination approximately 36 hours before arrival.

Beginning in Barcelona and concluding in Málaga, the eight-night sailing called at six ports: Mahón, Menorca; Castellón; Cartagena; Gibraltar; Motril; and Puerto Banús.

Windstar visited Castellón and Puerto Banús for the first time and returned to Motril after 18 years, having last called there in 2008.

“Our Mystery Cruises capture what Windstar is all about – a spirit of discovery, a sense of adventure, and the opportunity to experience the world in unexpected ways,” said Chris Prelog, president of Windstar Cruises.

Industry observers note that “There’s something special about stepping aboard without knowing exactly where the journey will take you and trusting that incredible experiences await. The enthusiasm we’ve seen for these sailings has been remarkable, and we’re excited to continue bringing this unique concept to upcoming destinations around the world.”.

Throughout the voyage, guests had the opportunity to experience the destinations through shore excursions showcasing the region’s history, culture and gastronomy.

Experiences ranged from coastal hiking adventures and explorations of historic fortresses to visits to local wineries, villages and regional culinary experiences.

As previously reported by Cruise Industry News, two additional Mystery Cruises are planned for 2027: the Northern Europe Mystery Cruise aboard the Star Pride and the Japan Mystery Cruises aboard the Star Seeker.

Breaking: Another bill to release Epstein files headed to House floor

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (579 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that massie will force another vote on releasing files in the Jeffrey Epstein case.
  • Thomas Massie, R-Ky., enters his final weeks in Congress, he is one step closer to another vote on legislation related to the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
  • A discharge petition led by Massie aimed at extracting more files from the Justice Department has now received enough support to force a vote on the House floor.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that massie will force another vote on releasing files in the Jeffrey Epstein case. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call file photo).

As Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., enters his final weeks in Congress, he is one step closer to another vote on legislation related to the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

A discharge petition led by Massie aimed at extracting more files from the Justice Department has now received enough support to force a vote on the House floor.

Rep. John Garamendi, D-Calif., was the decisive 218th signature on the discharge petition, a procedural tool allowing rank-and-file House members to register their support for a piece of legislation and circumvent leadership to force a vote. Massie and other supporters of the effort say the bill is a bid for transparency.

Earlier this week, Massie said his pitch to his colleagues was simple.

“They could be a hero if they sign it,” he said, as he chased down the final two signatures as the House returned from recess on Monday. Rep. Adam Smith, D-Wash., signed just before Garamendi.

Massie’s time left in office is ticking down after a challenger backed by President Donald Trump ousted him in his GOP primary earlier this year.

The petition marks the second push led by Massie to require the release of the Epstein files. Last fall, Massie and Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif., led a discharge petition on a bill dubbed the Epstein Files Transparency Act, which directed the Justice Department to publicly release documents in its possession related to Epstein and his associate Ghislaine Maxwell.

It has been revealed that the bill passed the House by a vote of 427-1 last November, and in the Senate a few days later. Trump signed the measure shortly afterward.

In a statement this summer, Massie mentioned he believes the Justice Department is still withholding more than 3 million files that it is required to release under the November 2025 law and is “maintaining heavy redactions” on others.

According to recent reports, the new bill would allow state attorneys general, local prosecutors and victims to sue the federal government for withholding such documents. It would also allow victims to privately view unredacted versions of any records that mention them.

Now that the newly introduced petition has reached 218 signatures, it must sit for seven legislative days before being called up by anyone who signed it. Last time around, Speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., scheduled a House vote on the initial Epstein bill before that ripening period was over, saying it was a foregone conclusion that the legislation would reach the floor.

According to recent reports, other Republicans who have signed on to the petition this year include Reps. Nancy Mace, R-S.C.; Ralph Norman, R-S.C., and Brian Fitzpatrick, R-Pa., none of whom will be returning next Congress. Rep. Lauren Boebert, R-Colo., backed the initial effort last fall, but her name did not appear on the petition this time.

Allies of the concern in Congress have faced pushback from Trump. While the president suggested during his 2024 reelection campaign that he was open to declassifying some Epstein documents, Trump then shifted gears, calling them a “hoax.”.

In a recent development, “Once you get to 218, you can never sign it," Massie said. "There's nobody left, no spots left. It goes straight to the floor, and then you can vote for it. But you were never part of the group that actually got it to the floor.".

In a recent development, budding geniuses deserve gifts that match their geeky interests. Whether it's robotics or chemistry or the mechanics of remote-control cars, the educational toy market is chock full of kits that help reinforce STEM (and STEAM) skills learned in school. They also give kids an off-screen activity that they’ll actually like doing.

Yet in the sea of options, there are only a handful of exceptional toys that truly stand out. We surveyed the landscape and handpicked the best of the best, guided by our familiarity with top brands and with our love of tinkering—an enriching activity people of all ages and genders love.

Here are our favorite gifts for boys (and any kids, really) who want to become the next generation of engineers, mechanics, carpenters, or astronomers.

It has been revealed that this interactive Lego set has a cool twist. Kids help Luigi solve a mystery through a garden that they build themselves. The set comes with four interactive figures that have a slew of reactions—it’s like an IRL video game.

Kids solve puzzle cards and design a 3D roller coaster around the solution. There are 60 different challenges and they can team up to play or stay entertained by themselves.

Industry observers note that space enthusiasts will love this Artemis build that mimics a rocket launch. The 632-piece set isn’t for the faint of heart but yields an amazing build that displays three separates stages of a real takeoff.

Industry observers note that the Snap Circuit set introduces kids to the wonderful world of electrical currents that keeps us running everyday. They can power a helicopter or fan, and even make a doorbell ring. There’s over 100 projects to choose from where they can create and learn along the way.

It has been revealed that this tiny robot has a significant personality to teach kids the basics of programming, algorithms, geometry, and more.It responds to voice cues and commands using the integrated app. Its versatility means kid will never get bored: Configure mechanical builds with the included set or program new behaviors and skills into the robot through coding.

It has been revealed that this fun intro to logic and and brain teaser puzzles is like a 3D version of Sudoku. Kids can play one of the 100 puzzle cards with each other or by themselves.

It has been revealed that this kit gives anyone the satisfaction of assembling a wearable mechanical hand. Once built, it can pick up objects using levers and the power of hydraulics, teaching kids about green energy in the process.

Sticky boogers, squishy eyeballs, and a handful of stringy guts to hold? Yes, please! This chemistry set lets kids create more than 40 truly disgusting experiments using included supplies and common household items. When it comes to slime, you can't lose.

Industry observers note that kids can tinker with this robot kit endlessly, turning it into one of twelve different configurations, each of which offers unique play. It runs on solar power or replaceable batteries, and includes 190 pieces and thorough instructions for building different animals and motions. Customers especially like Sillbird’s exceptional service when it comes to replacing faulty or missing parts.

Industry observers note that this 116-piece gear set from Learning Resources introduces young engineers to basic building skills. They can follow instructions to create pre-designed configurations, or have the freedom to make up their own. Most importantly, they’ll learn how gears and simple machines work—not bad for a toy designed for five-year-olds.

Kids learn basic automotive principals while building this iconic British race car, which features working wheels and doors, and moving pistons inside the V12 engine. It contains more than 700 pieces and there's the option of using printed instructions or Lego's building app for assembly.

It has been revealed that kids can create tons of fun electronic gadgets using this kit and have fun learning along the way. There are more than 300 projects to explore using the base grid and snap-together pieces, plus a helpful color manual for projects and instructions.

Sources indicate that get ready to launch objects up to 15 feet with a catapult, crossbow, and canon based on Leonardo Da Vinci's original designs. It comes with laser-cut pieces for three models that each take from 1 to 3 hours to build.

We like that this one is a logic puzzle and a fun marble run, all in one. Assemble the cubes so that when a marble is dropped from the top it makes it all the way to the bottom. Kids can create the pre-designed builds, or make their own mazes once they understand the concept.

Recent findings suggest that kids can choose to arrange this domino maze however they like in hundreds of different chain reactions or complete the increasingly difficult challenges laid out in the included cards. The goal is to build a chain from one point to another and hit the designated target. This gift features challenges that get harder as obstacles like stairs, walls, and blockers come into play.

This cardboard model kit adds some hands-on fun for fans of the Nintendo Switch. Kids build the customizable steering wheel, submarine, and airplane by following instructions on the Switch, then use their creations to play games with the console. Each model has built-in games and everything they need is included to build the sets, even things like tape.

Kids who love to tinker are sure to go bananas while unwrapping this gift. The 95-piece set comes with a wrench, screwdrivers, a hammer, and other tools, plus safety goggles and gloves. There’s also a tool belt and bag. The manufacturer recommends adult supervision for use.

A physics lesson, science experiment, and toy combined, the Water Rocket Kit can fly 90 feet into the air harnessing water and air pressure alone. Everything needed to construct it is included, except for a pump.

Forget about a boring day off from school. This book, compiled by Popular Mechanics editors, packs over 300 fun activities, interesting facts, and experiments in one place to always keep your kids entertained. It’s best for ages 8 to 12 and is a great book to keep on hand during long road trips and summer breaks.

Adults are sure to have a hard time keeping their hands off this awesome metal model airplane set. It comes with 258 pieces plus the tools they'll need to assemble it, and spans nearly 16 inches wide and 14 inches long when constructed. It’s recommended for kids ages 8 to 12.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Transcend Cruises has introduced its inaugural CEO-in-Residence Program, where its CEO Edie Rodriguez will spend a month sailing the Rhine onboard the Transcend Connect.

As a newly appointed CEO and board member, Rodriguez will run daily executive operations and leadership meetings from the ship between November 23 and December 22, 2026.

In what is stated to be the first time a cruise line CEO has spent an entire month onboard on either a river or cruise vessel, Rodriguez will meet with the onboard crew, charter clients and their guests and partners to help evolve Transcend’s brand strategy and product offering.

Corporate charters, MICE planners, travel advisors and affinity groups will also be able to connect and discuss customized itineraries and onboard experiences.

“Transcend Cruises was created to reimagine how groups come together on the rivers of Europe, turning every vessel into a customizable floating venue,” said Rodriguez.

“Setting up my office onboard for a month allows me stay close to our crew and operations and collaborate directly with clients and partners, and to experience the journeys just as they do and to better understand areas where we can improve as we continue to grow.”.

As the first charter-only river cruise firm with ships built exclusively for the group, Transcend welcomed its first ship, the Connect this summer, embarking on its first voyage on August 3, 2026.

Two additional ships are currently under construction, with plans for the fleet to reach four in 2028 and ultimately grow to 12 ships.

I’ve Tested Vacuums for Years. These Are the 6 Best Cordless Stick Vacs Under $300, Ranked.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The most powerful cordless stick vacuums will easily run you $500 or more, but in my experience, there are plenty of capable cleaners under $300.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that gear-obsessed editors choose every product we review. We may earn commission if you buy from a link. Why Trust Us?

The most powerful cordless stick vacuums will easily run you $500 or more, but in my experience, there are plenty of capable cleaners under $300. They may not rival the suction power, battery life, or features of their higher-priced counterparts, but many are perfectly capable of keeping up with typical household messes on hardwood, carpet, and every surface in between.

In a recent development, I’ve spent years testing vacuums for Popular Mechanics, and that experience informs a lot of my recommendations below. Some of these models have been through my own series of hands-on tests, while others made the cut based on my familiarity with their brands and product lines, along with research into their features and real-world performance. From budget-friendly everyday cleaners to options for pet owners, these are the best cordless vacuums that deliver the most for under $300.

The Shark PowerDetect is a feature-packed option for anyone who wants a cordless stick vacuum that does a lot of the thinking for them. The Detect mode automatically adjusts suction based on floor type and amount of debris, and a dual-roller floor head tackles tough messes on hardwood and carpet.

In a recent development, the hinged wand is great for cleaning under furniture and makes it a lot easier to reach hidden areas without having to bend down at all kinds of weird angles. It’s on the heavier side, and the long recharge time is a drawback, but strong pickup and smart features make it a good pick for whole-home cleaning.

Sources indicate that don’t let the price fool you: The Bissell PowerClean FurFinder is a strong and versatile cordless vacuum. It isn’t too heavy to carry between rooms, and the self-standing design means you don’t have to remount it or lay it flat any time you need to pause during your cleaning session.

It has been revealed that it has a tangle-free brush roll that does a great job picking up pet hair (as well as your own stray strands around the house). I also like the LED headlights that show hidden dirt, dust, and debris on floors and furniture. The attachments are great for above-floor cleaning, too. Battery life drops considerably when you crank up the suction power, so it’s best for maintenance cleaning.

Full Bissell PowerClean FurFinder Review.

The LVAC-300 packs cleaning power and everyday convenience into a lightweight machine. It’s easy to maneuver, and it transitions between hard floors, rugs, and low- to medium-pile carpet without scattering debris all over the floor. The tangle-resistant brush roll is a major pro for homes with pets or long hair, and five-stage filtration and washable filters are valuable additions.

It converts to a handheld vacuum cleaner with attachments for upholstery, stairs, and car interiors, and it uses a pleated mechanical HEPA filter with a dense arrangement of fibers to capture even the tiniest dust particles. The smaller dustbin and shorter runtime on max power might negatively impact your overall experience using this vacuum, but still, it’s versatile enough to take care of a variety of common household messes.

The Tineco Pure One Station 5 is the sibling to the Station 5 Pro that I’ve tested and still use to this day. And luckily, this more affordable model doesn’t cut key features that I love, such as the self-emptying and self-cleaning bagless docking station and green laser light for dust detection.

This model also has HEPA filtration and smart features. Internal sensors detect dust and adjust suction accordingly, and the anti-tangle brush roll helps prevent hair buildup. You get a shorter runtime with this model than you do with the Pro (estimated 70 minutes compared to the Pro’s 100), but the automated cleaning capability is hard to beat.

Recent findings suggest that the Dyson V8 is right at the edge of our $300 budget, but it’s a powerful option for homes with lots of carpeting or area rugs. I haven’t tried this specific model yet, but the motorbar floor cleaner is the same design that comes with other Dyson vacuums I’ve tried, such as the Dyson V15 Detect. It works well for hard floors, but I’ve found it particularly useful for dislodging embedded hair and debris from carpet fibers.

According to recent reports, the V8 comes with three attachments and converts into a handheld vacuum if you need more portability. Runtime is on the lower end for Dyson, but if you’re looking for a premium design without the premium price tag, the V8 is it.

Industry observers note that the Eureka ReactiSense 440 offers a number of features that make vacuuming less of a chore. It has dust detection sensors, automatic suction adjustment, floor head lights, and an anti-tangle brush roll with fins and a comb strip to prevent hair from getting wrapped around it.

I like that this model uses HEPA filtration to capture up to 99.7 percent of airborne particles and odors (which is great if you’re a pet owner). This model is lightweight and portable, converts to a handheld, and provides up to 60 minutes of runtime. Battery life will likely vary if you’re regularly cleaning at high power levels, but I’d reach for this vacuum for daily maintenance cleaning and quick pickups.

Amber is a Reviews Editor with bylines on Popular Mechanics, Runner’s World, Bicycling, and Best Products sites. Specializing in kitchen gadgets, small appliances, lifestyle, and consumer tech, she brings hands-on testing and a detail-oriented approach to every review. In her free time you can likely find her trading trinkets at an EDM festival, searching for hidden gems at thrift stores, or cuddling with her two cats.

  • Rand Paul, R-Ky., announced Wednesday he plans to serve as the top Republican on the Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee when Democrats take control of Congress next year.
  • The move clears the way for Senate Ethics Chairman James Lankford, R-Okla., to use his seniority to ascend to ranking Republican on the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, which Paul at the moment chairs, and touches off several other shifts at the top of other committees.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., leaves the Senate Republicans’ lunch in the Capitol on Tuesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call) (Bill Clark CQ Roll Call).

Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., announced Wednesday he plans to serve as the top Republican on the Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee when Democrats take control of Congress next year.

The move clears the way for Senate Ethics Chairman James Lankford, R-Okla., to use his seniority to ascend to ranking Republican on the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, which Paul at the moment chairs, and touches off several other shifts at the top of other committees.

In a recent development, the move fit in with Sen. Lisa Murkowski’s bid to use her seniority to succeed Senate Appropriations Chair Susan Collins, R-Maine, as top Republican on the Appropriations panel. If Paul did not go to the top spot on HELP, Murkowski, R-Alaska, would be next in line for that committee in the next Congress.

Murkowski is second in seniority on Appropriations to Collins, who was defeated for reelection. But she faces a potential challenge from Sen. Jerry Moran, R-Kan., who is next in line behind her.

Paul said in a press release that he aims to bring the same approach to the HELP Committee as he did as chairman of Homeland, where he said he “challenged entrenched bureaucracies, forced federal officials to answer for their actions, and pulled back the curtain on what Washington tried to keep hidden.”.

He cited calling Dr. Anthony Fauci before the committee to probe the former federal health official’s role in pandemic-related shutdowns and the origin of the COVID-19 virus, and releasing thousands of pages of pandemic-related documents. The panel voted in August to hold Fauci in criminal contempt of Congress for declining to answer questions about the pandemic during a highly charged hearing.

Related: Fauci could face criminal contempt charge following panel vote.

Paul, an ophthalmologist, remarked at HELP he will “stand against efforts to put Washington between Americans and their doctors, their children’s schools, and their paychecks.” He predicted “a rush toward socialism unlike anything we have seen” when the Democrat-controlled Congress convenes in January.

It has been revealed that lankford, in a separate statement, confirmed his interest in becoming the ranking member of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee. In many areas, he noted, the panel can work in a bipartisan manner, and over the past decade he “worked across the aisle to improve emergency communications in federal buildings, strengthen the United States Postal Service, increase federal cybersecurity preparedness, government transparency, and the use of artificial intelligence.”.

But he added that his job also would be to “push back on a [Democratic] majority that goes too far . . . Oversight is responsible, but obstruction is unacceptable.”.

In a recent development, lankford remarked he would work together with the likely committee chair, Sen. Maggie Hassan, D-N.H., “when we can agree and be a fierce opposition if there is an attempt to undercut our nation’s security.”.

Tech Report: Scott Colom elected Mississippi’s first Black senator since Reconstruction

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (750 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that mississippi Democrat Scott Colom, here at a news conference in Jackson on Nov.
  • Democrat Scott Colom has unseated Republican Sen.
  • The result is a stunning flip for Democrats in a deep-red state where they last won a Senate election in 1982, and it brings the Senate Democratic Caucus to at least 55 seats in the next Congress.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that mississippi Democrat Scott Colom, here at a news conference in Jackson on Nov. 4, has defeated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith. (Rogelio V. Solis/Getty Images).

Democrat Scott Colom has unseated Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith to become Mississippi’s first Black senator since Reconstruction.

The result is a stunning flip for Democrats in a deep-red state where they last won a Senate election in 1982, and it brings the Senate Democratic Caucus to at least 55 seats in the next Congress.

It has been revealed that colom was leading Hyde-Smith 49.2 percent to 48.7 percent — or by just over 4,600 votes out of more than 960,000 cast — when The Associated Press called the race Wednesday, a little over a week after Election Day. Ty Pinkins, the 2024 Democratic Senate nominee who ran as an independent this year, had 2 percent.

In recent days, as absentee and provisional ballots were counted, Colom had all but declared victory, repeatedly saying that Hyde-Smith had no path to victory.

“I'll work every day in the U.S. Senate to build a future that generations of Mississippians can be just as proud to call home,” he posted Monday on social media.

With his victory, Colom joins several other Democrats who flipped seats in deep-red states, including Texas’ James Talarico, Kansas’ Adam Hamilton and South Carolina’s Annie Andrews. Democrats have so far flipped eight Senate seats to win control of the chamber, overcoming a difficult Senate map and giving them their largest majority in the chamber since 2011.

In a recent development, that majority could expand further if Democrats flip the Senate seat in Alaska, where former Rep. Mary Peltola narrowly leads Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan.

Republicans have dominated Senate elections in Mississippi in recent decades. The last Democrat to be elected senator in the Magnolia State was John C. Stennis, who won his sixth full and final term in 1982. Colom will be the third Black man to serve as a Mississippi senator after Republicans Hiram Revels and Blanche Bruce during Reconstruction.

While Revels and Bruce, who left office in 1881, were elected by the state Legislature, Colom will be the first Black senator elected directly by voters.

Colom has served as a district attorney for four counties in northeast Mississippi since 2016. President Joe Biden nominated him for a federal district judgeship in 2022, but Hyde-Smith effectively blocked his nomination by not returning a so-called blue slip, a Senate Judiciary Committee tradition that lets senators derail district judge nominees in their home states.

Senate Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer stated last week that he’d had Colom in his sights for several years as a potential Senate candidate, including for a race against the state’s senior senator, Republican Roger Wicker.

“I had Scott Colom and his father come to my house, and I served them a nice little brunch or something. I said, ‘You got to run,’” the Newly introduced York Democrat recalled to MS NOW. “They were smarter than me. This was four years ago. They said, ‘We don’t want to run this time, but we know that Hyde-[Smith], the incumbent, is so weak, we could beat her.’”.

Sources indicate that still, the Mississippi race didn’t capture as much national attention as other Senate contests until the closing weeks of the campaign. A trio of Black senators, Angela Alsobrooks of Maryland, Lisa Blunt Rochester of Delaware and Cory Booker of New Jersey, all campaigned with Colom throughout the summer and fall. Key national figures, including former President Bill Clinton, former Vice President Kamala Harris and former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg, also stumped for him in October.

Recent findings suggest that colom’s campaign engaged voters with quirky ads and unconventional forms of outreach, including meeting with people lining up to attend a Trump rally. One ad that went viral played on Hyde Smith saying earlier this year that people had “so many proteins to choose from” when asked about rising beef prices.

Industry observers note that “Pick another protein?” says a man in the ad. “I’d rather pick another senator instead.”.

In a recent development, major Democratic outside groups made a late play in the state, with WinSenate, which is affiliated with Senate Democrats’ top super PAC, investing $2.2 million. The Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee spent $500,000 on a coordinated ad buy late last month.

Industry observers note that the pro-Republican Senate Leadership Fund dropped $1.7 million on the race, and Trump headlined a rally for Hyde-Smith on Oct. 26.

#88510. 21 Best Places to Visit in December in the USA

📅 31 Oct 2025 • ⏱️ 16m • 📚 Deep Dive (3294 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Theplanetd ↗ Open Full Page

21 Best Places to Visit in December in the USA

📅 31 Oct 2025 | ⏱️ 16 min read (3294 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theplanetd

⏱️ ~16 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that we’ll never forget the first time we visited New York City in December.
  • In a recent development, but December travel isn’t just about snow and Santa.
  • Industry observers note that in fact, we’ve been to almost all 50 states and spent a lot of winters trying to find the most fun destinations and best weather.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that we’ll never forget the first time we visited New York City in December. We’d seen it in movies, but standing there, seeing the Rockefeller Center tree all lit up for the first time, with skaters below and festive music in the air… it was pure magic.

In a recent development, but December travel isn’t just about snow and Santa. We’ve also spent the holidays escaping to the warmth, trading snow boots for flip-flops.

Industry observers note that in fact, we’ve been to almost all 50 states and spent a lot of winters trying to find the most fun destinations and best weather. We’ve done so many road trips in the USA and flown almost everywhere, trying to find the best places to either escape the snow or enjoy the winter, you would think we are obsessed. And we want to share all of that knowledge with you.

In a recent development, if you’re looking for the perfect winter getaway, you have a clear choice: either lean into the winter magic or escape it completely. Are you dreaming of a warm-weather escape with sunshine and sand, or a storybook Christmas town that looks like a real-life snow globe?

Industry observers note that based on all those experiences, we’ve put together this list of our favourite places to visit. Whether you’re looking for a festive city, a snowy mountain, or a sunny beach, we’ll help you find the perfect spot.

Here is a quick look at some of the best places for a December getaway in the USA, from festive winter wonderlands to sunny escapes.

Recent findings suggest that december is a month of pure magic and festive energy. It’s the perfect time to use up that last bit of vacation time for the year. The biggest draw is the distinct choice it offers: You can either dive head-first into a winter wonderland, complete with snow and holiday markets, or you can completely escape the cold weather and find yourself on a sunny beach. It’s a month of festive celebrations, incredible decorations, and finding the perfect atmosphere to end the year.

If you’re anything like us, sometimes the best gift in December is a break from the cold. Trust us, we know after living in Toronto, Canada. Those winters are brutal. These are our favourite spots to find sunshine and warm weather, where you can trade your winter coat for a light jacket or even a swimsuit.

We love the laid-back, quirky vibe of Key West, and it’s even more special in December. We have a great memory of biking around the island, seeing the historic inns draped in holiday lights, and then ending the day at Mallory Square for the sunset celebration. It’s a perfect escape from the cold.

It has been revealed that why Visit in December: This is the perfect time to visit. The summer humidity is gone, the weather is sunny and warm (often in the high 70s), and the risk of hurricanes is very low. The whole island is in a festive spirit, with unique events like the “Bight Before Christmas” boat parade.

Where to Stay: We recommend finding a guesthouse or inn in the historic Old Town to be close to the action.

Recent findings suggest that we once went to a holiday luau in Ka’anapali, and it’s an experience we’ll never forget. You’re eating kalua pork and sipping a mai tai, watching a beautiful hula performance… and then Santa Claus arrives on an outrigger canoe. It was the perfect, uniquely Hawaiian way to get into the festive spirit.

In a recent development, why Visit in December: You get tropical weather, festive holiday luaus, and it’s the official start of the humpback whale watching season. Be aware that this is a popular time, especially around Christmas, so prices can be high and you’ll need to book in advance.

Where to Stay: Look to the resorts in Wailea or Ka’anapali for a classic Maui experience.

We’ll always remember snorkeling the underwater trail at Trunk Bay in St. John. The water was so calm and clear, and seeing all the colourful fish felt a world away from the snow back home. That’s the magic of a Caribbean trip in December, and the USVI makes it so easy for American travelers.

Industry observers note that why Visit in December: It’s the start of the dry season, with fantastic weather and warm, clear water. You get a full-on tropical, warm-weather Christmas experience, all without needing a passport.

Sources indicate that where to Stay: You can choose from large resorts in St. Thomas or more eco-friendly villas and lodges in St. John.

In a recent development, we were not prepared for how magical St. Augustine is in December. We took one of the Old Town trolley tours at night, and seeing the entire historic city, from the old Spanish architecture to the palm trees, draped in millions of white lights… it was breathtaking. It’s a holiday light display unlike any other.

It has been revealed that why Visit in December: The famous “Nights of Lights” festival. The entire city is illuminated, and the mild Florida weather is perfect for walking around and enjoying the atmosphere. It’s one of the most festive and warm places you can visit.

Where to Stay: We recommend a historic inn or bed & breakfast in the downtown district to be within walking distance of all the lights.

While Maui is our go-to for a resort escape, Honolulu is where you go for a vibrant, city-meets-beach holiday. We loved seeing the massive Santa surfing with his reindeer in the fountain at the Iolani Palace. The whole city has this amazing “Mele Kalikimaka” (Merry Christmas) spirit.

Why Visit in December: It’s the perfect blend of warm beach weather, world-class shopping, and festive displays. It’s also a significant month for history, with the memorial events at Pearl Harbor.

Where to Stay: Waikiki has a huge range of hotels, from historic beachfront properties to modern high-rises.

Recent findings suggest that if your idea of a winter getaway is to truly get away from everything, the crowds, the noise, the stress, then South Padre is a perfect choice. We spent a week there, and our days consisted of long, quiet walks on the beach. It was a total reset and the perfect way to escape the winter blues.

Why Visit in December: The weather is mild, and the crowds are gone. It’s one of the warmest places in Texas and offers a simple, relaxing beach vacation without the high prices or holiday chaos of other destinations.

Where to Stay: You’ll find many beachfront condos and hotels offering great off-season rates.

We thought we knew desert holiday lights, but the “Las Noches de las Luminarias” at the Desert Botanical Garden in Phoenix is on another level. Walking the garden paths lit by thousands of hand-lit luminaria bags, with musicians playing, was a top-tier holiday experience.

Why Visit in December: You get two trips in one: perfect, sunny weather for outdoor adventures like hiking during the day, and stunning, sophisticated holiday light displays at night.

Where to Stay: Choose from upscale resorts in Scottsdale or stylish hotels in downtown Phoenix.

In a recent development, sometimes, the warm weather destinations just won’t cut it, especially if you are looking for that winter wonderland feel. So, this section is for travellers who want to dive head-first into the holiday spirit. These are the cities and towns that go all-out for December, with millions of lights, Christmas markets, and an atmosphere of pure magic.

We’ve visited NYC many times, but there’s a specific energy in December. We grabbed hot chocolates and walked through the Bryant Park Winter Village, watching the ice skaters zip around the rink under the lights of the surrounding skyscrapers. It felt like being in the opening scene of a holiday movie. There is nothing like Fresh York City at Christmas.

Why Visit in December: It is the quintessential American Christmas destination. From the iconic tree to the world-famous window displays, the entire city is on a different level of festive.

Where to Stay: Midtown is convenient for seeing the main holiday sights, but we also love the West Village for its cosy, neighbourhood feel.

Industry observers note that we’d heard Leavenworth was a “Christmas Town,” but we weren’t prepared for the reality. We visited during the Village of Lights festival, and walking through the snow-covered Bavarian-style village while every single building was covered in over half a million lights… it’s not an exaggeration. It’s the closest we’ve ever felt to being inside a real-life snow globe.

Sources indicate that why Visit in December: The entire town transforms into a “Hallmark movie” Christmas village. It’s a full-immersion holiday experience with carolers, festive food, and incredible decorations.

Where to Stay: Book a Bavarian-style lodge or inn right in the village. You must book many months in advance for December.

In a recent development, we love Asheville, but visiting in December is all about the Biltmore Estate. We took the candlelight evening tour, and seeing the main banquet hall with its 35-foot tree, fireplaces roaring, and carolers singing… it felt like we’d stepped back in time into a Gilded Age Christmas party.

Industry observers note that why Visit in December: Christmas at Biltmore is one of the most iconic holiday events in the country. The city itself is a cosy mountain retreat, and the Blue Ridge Mountains are just beautiful with a dusting of snow.

Where to Stay: You can stay on the Biltmore Estate for the full experience or choose a boutique hotel downtown.

Here are the remaining destinations for the “Best Christmas Towns & Festive Cities” section, all written with unique, December-focused content.

We’ve visited a lot of Christmas markets, but visiting the one in Bethlehem, known as “Christmas City USA”, just felt right. We sipped hot cider and browsed the stalls in the old quarter, and you can feel the city’s 250+ years of Christmas tradition. The whole place is lit by the glow of a giant Moravian star on the hillside.

Why Visit in December: This is Christmas City USA. It was nicknamed this on Christmas Eve, 1741. It offers one of the most authentic and historic holiday experiences in the country, blending its Moravian heritage with a European-style Christkindlmarkt.

Where to Stay: Look for a hotel or inn in the historic downtown area to be close to the festivities.

Recent findings suggest that walking into Solvang in December felt like we’d been transported to a Danish village during its Julefest celebration. We spent the day exploring the half-timbered buildings, windmills, and bakeries, all decorated for the holidays. It’s such a unique and charming way to experience a winter getaway in the middle of California.

Why Visit in December: The town’s month-long “Julefest” (Yule-fest) celebration is in full swing. It’s a one-of-a-kind Danish-style Christmas with parades, markets, and, of course, delicious European pastries.

Where to Stay: Choose one of the charming Danish-themed inns right in the village to be in the middle of the Julefest activities.

We had to see the “Christmas Capital of Texas” for ourselves, and it did not disappoint. The entire historic Main Street is transformed. We loved seeing the vintage railroad, which becomes the “North Pole Express” for the month. They take the “Christmas Capital” title seriously; there are over 1,400 events in 40 days.

Sources indicate that why Visit in December: It is the officially designated “Christmas Capital of Texas”. The sheer number of festive events, light displays, and activities is staggering, making it a top-tier destination for families and holiday lovers.

Where to Stay: The Gaylord Texan Resort is an attraction in itself, or you can stay near the Historic Main Street to be close to the events.

A Newly introduced Orleans Christmas is an experience all its own. We did a “Reveillon Dinner,” a modern take on a Creole holiday tradition, and it was one of the most memorable meals we’ve ever had. Afterwards, we walked to Jackson Square to see the St. Louis Cathedral all lit up while carolers sang.

Sources indicate that why Visit in December: You get to experience unique Creole Christmas traditions you won’t find anywhere else. The weather is mild, the food is incredible, and the city’s lobbies (like at The Roosevelt) have some of the most elegant decorations we’ve seen.

Where to Stay: We recommend a hotel in the French Quarter to be in the middle of the action and see the decorated lobbies.

Industry observers note that we went to Natchitoches (pronounced Nak-a-tish) specifically for its Christmas Festival, and it was a total joy. It’s one of the oldest and biggest in the country. The whole city, which is the oldest in Louisiana, lights up with over 300,000 lights along the Cane River, and the weekly fireworks shows are fantastic.

Why Visit in December: It hosts one of the oldest and most celebrated holiday festivals in the US, running for six weeks. It’s a classic, Southern Christmas experience in a beautiful historic district.

Where to Stay: Book a room at a historic bed & breakfast in the downtown area.

In a recent development, visiting Colonial Williamsburg in December felt like walking through a living history Christmas card. We joined a candlelight tour, and seeing the historic buildings lit by real candles in the windows, with carolers in period costumes and the smell of woodsmoke in the air… it was absolutely magical.

Why Visit in December: You get to experience a traditional, 18th-century “Colonial Christmas”. The decorations are all-natural (no plastic lights), and the atmosphere is incredibly authentic and charming.

Where to Stay: Stay in one of the historic Colonial Houses or a tavern right in the restored area for the full immersive experience.

Here is the final category of destinations. This section is all about embracing the snow and finding that perfect winter wonderland.

For many, holiday season travel is all about finding that perfect, snowy scene. These are the places to go for world-class skiing, cosy lodges, and that magical feeling of a true winter escape.

Sources indicate that we’ll always remember our first “après-ski” in Aspen. We had spent the day on the mountain hitting fresh powder whenever we got the chance, and as the sun went down, the sky lit up with this incredible pink and orange light they call “Aspenglow.” Sitting by a fire, enjoying a glass of Christmas cheer, and watching the snow fall on the historic town, it just felt like the peak of a luxury winter trip.

According to recent reports, why Visit in December: It’s one of the world’s most famous upscale ski destinations, and the town is just as much an attraction as the mountains. The festive atmosphere, high-end shops, and restaurants are all decked out for the holidays.

Where to Stay: Aspen is known for its luxury hotels and ski-in/ski-out resorts.

One of our favourite things about Park City is its history. We loved skiing down to the historic Main Street, popping off our skis, and walking straight into a saloon that’s been there since the silver mining days. It feels like a real Western town, not just a ski resort.

In a recent development, why Visit in December: It’s a historic mountain town with two world-class ski resorts (Park City and Deer Valley). The historic Main Street is incredibly charming, and the “Snow Globe Stroll” features life-sized snow globes you can walk through.

Where to Stay: You can find ski-in/ski-out hotels or stay at an inn on the historic Main Street.

Jackson Hole in December is just dramatic. We took a sleigh ride through the National Elk Refuge, and seeing thousands of elk gathered against the backdrop of the snow-covered Teton mountains… it was a powerful and wild winter experience we’ve never forgotten.

Sources indicate that why Visit in December: It’s the perfect mix of rugged “cowboy Christmas” charm and some of the most challenging ski terrain in North America. The town square, with its famous antler arches, is beautifully lit for the holidays.

Where to Stay: Stay at a slopeside resort in Teton Village or in a hotel in the town of Jackson.

According to recent reports, we love Whitefish because it feels like a real, down-to-earth ski town. We spent a day snowshoeing in nearby Glacier National Park, enjoying the total silence and incredible snowy landscapes, and then came back to town for a casual dinner. It’s all the beauty, without the glitz. Just what we were looking for in a winter vacation.

Why Visit in December: It’s a laid-back, charming mountain town with a top-rated ski resort and stunning scenery. It’s also right next to Glacier National Park, which is a spectacular place to explore in the winter.

Where to Stay: You can find lodges on the mountain or stay in one of the friendly inns in downtown Whitefish.

This was a trip purely for the fun of it, and it was 100% worth it. You drive down streets named “Santa Claus Lane” and “St. Nicholas Drive,” the streetlights are shaped like candy canes, and you can visit the Santa Claus House and see his reindeer. It’s a surreal and joyful experience.

Why Visit in December: It’s the ultimate Christmas fantasy come to life. The entire town is Christmas-themed, 365 days a year, but it’s most magical in December with real snow on the ground and the added bonus of possibly seeing the Northern Lights.

Where to Stay: North Pole is very small; most visitors stay in the nearby city of Fairbanks, which has a wide range of hotels.

In a recent development, for the best warm weather, your top choices are Southern Florida (like Key West), Hawaii (like Maui and Honolulu), and the desert Southwest (like Phoenix and Palm Springs). The U.S. Virgin Islands are also a fantastic passport-free tropical option.

Industry observers note that leavenworth, Washington, is often considered the ultimate “Christmas town” as it looks just like a Bavarian snow globe. Other top choices include Bethlehem, PA (known as “Christmas City USA”), Solvang, CA (for a Danish-style Julefest), and Grapevine, TX (the “Christmas Capital of Texas”).

Yes, but it depends on the park. It’s the perfect time to visit desert parks like Death Valley, Everglades, and Big Bend, where summer heat is unbearable. However, many mountain parks like Glacier, Yellowstone, and parts of Yosemite are mostly inaccessible due to heavy snow and road closures.

Recent findings suggest that you are almost guaranteed to find snow in the mountain towns of the Rockies, like Aspen, CO, Park City, UT, and Jackson Hole, WY. You’ll also find snow in the Cascade Mountains (like Leavenworth, WA), Alaska, and the mountains around Lake Tahoe.

December is a magical month to travel. Whether you’re chasing the sun, seeking out that perfect snowy scene, or looking for a town that’s full of holiday magic, the US has the perfect spot for you.

According to recent reports, we hope this list, based on our own winter travels, helps you plan your next getaway. Save this on Pinterest for your holiday planning! Where is your favourite place to go in December?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Azamara Quest is presently wrapping up a drydock in Elefsis to become the first ship to undergo refurbishment as part of the Azamara Forward program.

After wrapping up its summer season in Piraeus, the vessel arrived at a Greek shipyard on October 31, 2026.

As part of the project, the 2000-built ship is getting a new deck with more staterooms, in addition to refreshed public rooms, as well as new venues, such as the Atlas Bar.

All staterooms are also being updated with new finishes, improved lighting and design details aimed at enhancing comfort.

The newly introduced Penthouse Deck adds 12 additional suites. The new premium staterooms will also introduce two new suite categories to the manufacturer’s fleet: Panorama and Grandview.

“We have designed these suites to have that calming, welcoming environment of a home away from home feeling for our guests,” remarked Martha Brabham, vice president of design and revitalization.

Recent findings suggest that “So we would love our guests to enjoy the color scheme, the palette. We curated the elements in the room to really immerse you into that ocean experience.”.

Upon completion of the enhancements, the Azamara Quest is now scheduled to welcome guests back on November 26, 2026.

The ship is then set to offer itineraries in the Mediterranean, the Atlantic and the Caribbean before kicking off Azamara’s annual World Cruise in 2027.

“As the ship undergoes drydock, there’s a lot of work happening behind the scenes to bring Azamara Forward to life,” Azamara stated in a status upgrade.

“From refreshed spaces to thoughtful enhancements throughout the ship, every detail is coming together as the transformation takes shape,” the company added.

All ships in the firm’s fleet are scheduled to undergo refurbishments as part of the Azamara Forward program.

The Azamara Onward will undergo the refit next, entering drydock in late 2027, followed by the Azamara Journey in late 2028.
